title: Monitoring and Diagnostics
description: Use logs, metrics, and alerts to keep an eye on your ASP.NET Core app running in App Service.

data.text: App Service provides built-in logging, metrics, and diagnostic tools. For deeper telemetry, Application Insights is covered in a later module.

data.title: Enable web server logging and application logging
data.content: Use the Azure CLI to turn on logs without leaving the terminal.
data.code:
az webapp log config \
  --name azure-for-aspnet-demo \
  --resource-group azure-for-aspnet-rg \
  --application-logging true \
  --webserver-logging true \
  --detailed-error-messages true \
  --failed-request-tracing true

data.text: Use the Azure CLI to stream logs from the running app in real time.

data.title: Stream logs from App Service
data.content: Run this in a dedicated terminal window while you exercise the app.
data.code:
az webapp log tail \
  --name azure-for-aspnet-demo \
  --resource-group azure-for-aspnet-rg

items: In the Azure portal, open **Metrics** and choose CPU Time, Memory Working Set, or HTTP 5xx errors
Create an alert rule that emails you when CPU Time exceeds a threshold
Use **Diagnose and solve problems** for automated troubleshooting

data.title: Add health checks and observe them in Azure
data.description: ASP.NET Core has built-in health checks that work well with App Service.
steps: Browse the app and trigger an error
Stream logs with `az webapp log tail`
data.expectedOutcome: You see request logs and exceptions in the live log stream.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: App Service logs include web server logs, application logs, and failed request traces
Log streaming is useful during development and incident response
Metrics and alerts reduce mean time to detection
Health checks give App Service a simple readiness endpoint
data.takeaway: Basic App Service diagnostics are enough for early production, and they integrate cleanly with ASP.NET Core health checks.
